questions.question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.

options.text: Alka bought new pair of shoes for the party.
He was an honest engineer by profession.
Suhas has a younger brother and an elder sister.
It was a huge zoo with an elephant enclosure.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Alka bought new pair of shoes for the party.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "Alka bought new pair of shoes for the party" contains a grammatical error.
 
• The phrase "new pair of shoes" is incorrect because it lacks the article "a" before "new."
 
• In English, when referring to a singular countable noun modified by an adjective, an article such as "a" or "an" is required.

Correct sentence: *Alka bought **a new pair of shoes** for the party.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He was an honest engineer by profession." 
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct. The article "an" is correctly used before the word "honest," as "honest" starts with a vowel sound.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Suhas has a younger brother and an elder sister." 
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct. The articles "a" and "an" are correctly used before "younger brother" and "elder sister," respectively.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "It was a huge zoo with an elephant enclosure." 
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct. The article "an" is correctly used before "elephant," as it starts with a vowel sound.

questions.question:
Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

His remarks __made the matter worse.__

options.text: Killed two birds with one stone

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Added fuel to the fire**.

__
 
• The phrase **"Added fuel to the fire"** means to make a bad situation worse by doing or saying something that causes more anger or difficulty. (आग में घी डालना)

 
 
• **Example:** Instead of calming the argument, his sarcastic comment only added fuel to the fire.
 
 
 
• The sentence "His remarks made the matter worse" implies that his remarks intensified the problem, which perfectly aligns with the idiom "added fuel to the fire." (आग में घी डालने जैसा काम किया।)

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Added fuel to the fire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Spilled the beans** (राज खोल देना): To reveal a secret or confidential information unintentionally or intentionally.

 
 
• **Example:** She accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party.
 
 
 
• **Made a splash** (धूम मचाना): To attract a lot of attention or make a big impression.
 
 
• **Example:** The new fashion designer made a splash with her innovative designs.
 
 
 
• **Killed two birds with one stone** (एक तीर से दो निशाने): To accomplish two objectives with a single action.
 
 
• **Example:** By attending the conference, he killed two birds with one stone: he networked with professionals and learned new skills.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The storm caused extensive damage to homes, __________ many families homeless.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**leaving**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb "**leaving**" is the correct choice because it is a participle that indicates the result of the action described in the first part of the sentence.
 
• The sentence describes a cause-and-effect relationship: the storm caused damage, resulting in families becoming homeless. Hence, "**leaving**" is the appropriate word to convey this.
 
• **Options 1, 2,** and **3** are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The storm caused extensive damage to homes, **leaving**__ many families homeless."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "to leave"** is incorrect because it breaks the sentence structure and does not fit the cause-and-effect relationship.
 
• **Option 2: "leave"** is incorrect because it is not in the participle form, which is required here.
 
• **Option 3: "is left"** is incorrect as it changes the meaning of the sentence and does not convey the intended result.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He is / an expert / in / an English literature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. an English literature .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the segment **"an English literature"**.
 
• The article **"an"** is incorrect when referring to the subject "literature" in this context. The article **"an"** is used before words starting with a vowel sound, but it is not suitable for uncountable nouns like "literature."
 
• Instead, the correct usage should be **"English literature"** without any article, as "literature" is a general, uncountable noun.

Correct sentence: *He is an expert in English literature.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles and Nouns:**

 
 
• Articles like **"a"** and **"an"** are used with singular, countable nouns. For example: "a book," "an apple."
 
• Uncountable nouns (like "literature," "information," "furniture") do not take an article in general usage unless specified (e.g., "the literature of the 19th century").
 
 
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:**
 
 
• Ensure that the subject and verb in a sentence agree in number (singular/plural).
